headline: Cognition has released SWE-2, a coding model it says comes within one point of Fable 5.1 on a coding test at 64% lower cost.
score_reason: Kept: a real release from a known coding-agent company, but all results are its own.
importance_line: Software teams get a cheaper option that Cognition says nears the top of coding-agent performance, but the scores and cost comparisons are the company's own and not independently verified.
summary: Cognition, whose coding tools include Devin, says in its launch post that SWE-2 scored 50.0% on the FrontierCode 1.1 Main coding test, within one point of Fable 5.1 at 64% lower cost, and is available from today in Devin Desktop and its command-line tool, with Devin Web and Fusion being rolled out. The model was built by further training Kimi K3, a 2.8-trillion-parameter model, using reinforcement learning (training by trial and reward) that also penalises expensive solutions.
notes: Read the Cognition post (first 16,000 characters). Status CONFIRMED covers the release; all benchmark figures are Cognition's claims.
